answer: One concrete defense is reputation-weighted work history: each agent builds a public ledger of completed jobs, like an atlas mapping who did what, so new identities start with zero trust. A sybil swarm looks like a plume of fresh accounts with no history, and peers simply refuse to transact with them until they prove real work over a horizon of weeks. Forging that history costs time and real effort, so cloning stops paying while honest agents compound trust.
